item.title: Meta Changes AI Chatbot Prompt Suggestions After Digging for Personal Information
item.description:
Meta Changes AI Chatbot Prompt Suggestions After Digging for Personal Information

Meta is making changes to the suggested prompts of its AI chatbot following a viral video that showed the assistant seeking personal information about a user’s young daughters.

🔍 Overview

The changes come after Instagram user Kalie Robins posted a video detailing an invasive prompt presented by Meta AI. After cross-posting a video of her and her child singing in a car to Facebook, the prompt “Who is the child passenger?” appeared beneath the clip.

When Robins selected the prompt, Meta AI gathered information about her daughters from her previous posts, as well as posts shared by her relatives. The assistant then:

  • Suggested additional prompts asking about her children’s ages.
  • Suggested prompts asking where Robins lives with her family.
  • Showed photos of her daughters posted to the platform, including one Robins claims she deleted years ago.

⚙️ Key details

In a statement, Meta spokesperson Dina El-Kassaby stated that the company “missed the mark,” adding that “the feature never should have prompted the individual with questions like that.”

El-Kassaby provided several clarifications regarding the incident and the feature’s mechanics:

  • Fix implemented: Meta has resolved the issue causing Meta AI to suggest prompts related to personal topics.
  • Feature intent: The feature was designed to help users obtain more information about topics or posts that interest them.
  • Information access: When a user clicks a prompt, the generated response is based entirely on information the user already has access to. In this specific case, El-Kassaby noted that Meta AI may have pulled from videos where Robins named her children.

🌐 Context and Integration

Meta has integrated its AI assistant across its primary platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger, where it can answer questions, write posts, and generate images. This is not the first time Meta has adjusted its AI features due to user response; in July, the company pulled a feature that allowed users to create AI deepfakes of other Instagram users after facing fierce backlash.

#MetaAI #Privacy #SocialMedia #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: Meta says it’s changing AI suggestions after posing invasive personal questions

item.title: AIWriteX Updates Content Creation Tool with Multi-Agent Framework and Expanded Platform Support
item.description:
AIWriteX Updates Content Creation Tool with Multi-Agent Framework and Expanded Platform Support

AIWriteX has introduced a significant update to its content generation and management platform, integrating a multi-agent framework and expanding automation capabilities across various social media channels. The update focuses on simplifying content workflows through natural language control and multi-platform synchronization.

🧩 How it works

The platform’s architecture is now driven by the CrewAI multi-agent framework, which employs clear role division to handle complex tasks. It is supported by AIForge, a real-time information engine that uses multi-strategy searching to gather data and analyze competitors.

Users can manage the platform through several control methods:

  • Mobile bot integration for QQ, DingTalk, Feishu, Discord, and Telegram.
  • Support for fixed commands and natural language interaction to complete workflows.
  • A visualization interface for full management of configurations, templates, articles, and illustrations.

⚙️ Key details

AIWriteX supports content distribution and management across multiple major platforms with specific feature sets:

Platform Supported Features
WeChat Official Account Graphics, stickers, drafts, auto-publish, long images, TXT/MD, HTML templates, batch generation
Xiaohongshu Graphic messages, drafts, auto-publish, long images, style adaptation
Baijiahao Graphics, stickers, drafts, auto-publish, long images, TXT/MD, HTML templates
今日头条 (Toutiao) Graphics, stickers, drafts, auto-publish, long images, TXT/MD, HTML templates
番茄小说 (Fanqie Fiction) Novel publishing, auto-volume creation, drafts, auto-publish, TXT
Weibo Graphics, auto-publish, TXT/MD, hotspot data aggregation

🔍 Overview

The update includes extensive design and analysis tools to improve content quality and relevance:

  • Design Templates: 9 categories of Markdown templates with 23 styles and 9 categories of image templates with 40 options.
  • Style Presets: 21 built-in illustration style presets for immediate use without parameter adjustment.
  • Hotspot Analysis: Automated scraping of trending topics from Weibo, Douyin, and Xiaohongshu with depth analysis for generating outlines and writing guidance.
  • Trend Prediction: Capabilities to forecast traffic trends for the upcoming 12 hours.
  • Formatting: Automatic typesetting for WeChat, Xiaohongshu, and Douyin styles, with Markdown and HTML export options.

💡 Why it matters

The update introduces a “De-AI” optimization engine that uses anti-detection and natural polishing to create a human-like writing style. Additionally, the platform supports automated WeChat management, including downloading all articles from specific accounts and following accounts for new post notifications. One-click publishing now supports scheduled tasks and multi-account management to streamline high-volume content production across diverse creative engines like style conversion and role-playing.

#AIWriteX #CrewAI #ContentAutomation #MultiAgentSystems #SocialMedia

Source: iniwap/AIWriteX

item.title: C³T Transformer Enables Counterfactual Causal Reasoning of Sentiment Shifts in Social Media Threads
item.description:
C³T Transformer Enables Counterfactual Causal Reasoning of Sentiment Shifts in Social Media Threads

A new paper titled C$^{3}$T: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Sentiment Shifts in Social‑Media Conversation Trees was submitted on 2 Sep 2026 to the Computer Science > Computation and Language category. The work tackles how sentiment changes throughout branching reply trees on social media, especially in rumor‑centric conversations.

🔍 Overview

  • Sentiment does not only vary across individual posts; it shifts as users react to claims, corrections, evidence, and hostility within a thread.
  • The authors treat discourse moves such as denial/correction, evidence/link, and toxicity/attack as candidate interventions.
  • Three research questions are posed:
    1. What sentiment does a reply express?
    2. Does the reply’s sentiment shift relative to its parent?
    3. Which prior message most plausibly drove the reply’s sentiment?

🧩 How it works

  • CaSiRe layer: A causal sentiment reasoning layer added to public rumor conversation datasets. It provides:
    • Post‑level sentiment labels
    • Parent‑child shift labels
    • Calibrated multi‑label intervention tags
    • Explicit causal‑source annotations
  • C$^{3}$T model (Counterfactual Causal Conversation Transformer):
    • Thread‑structured temporal architecture
    • Jointly predicts node sentiment and shift labels
    • Learns sparse ancestor attribution
    • Supports counterfactual queries by toggling intervention embeddings on or off to estimate potential outcomes

⚙️ Key Findings

  • Under an event‑level split, C$^{3}$T outperforms text‑only, graph‑based, and temporal baselines in out‑of‑event robustness and attribution accuracy.
  • Interpretable model effects show that:
    • Denials/corrections and evidence tend to reduce downstream negativity.
    • Toxicity tends to increase downstream negativity.
  • Open‑weight LLM prompting baselines benefit from added conversational context, but their attribution remains less reliable than the structure‑aware counterfactual approach.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a systematic way to attribute sentiment shifts to specific prior messages in complex conversation trees.
  • Enables researchers and platform moderators to simulate “what‑if” scenarios by turning interventions on or off, helping to assess potential mitigation strategies for harmful discourse.

The work demonstrates the value of combining causal reasoning with transformer‑based modeling for nuanced social‑media sentiment analysis.

#sentimentanalysis #causalAI #socialmedia #nlp

Source: C$^{3}$T: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Sentiment Shifts in Social-Media Conversation Trees

item.title: Instagram to Limit Reach of Unlabeled AI-Generated Profiles
item.description:
Instagram to Limit Reach of Unlabeled AI-Generated Profiles

Instagram is implementing new measures to address the rise of fake AI-influencer accounts that have become increasingly difficult to detect.

⚙️ Key details

Instagram is introducing the following changes to identify AI-generated personas:

  • Label Update: The “AI creator” label is being renamed to “AI-generated profile” to clarify when a profile features an AI-generated person rather than a real human being.
  • Enforcement: The platform will identify accounts that fail to self-label their AI-generated profiles.
  • Penalties: Accounts that do not self-label will have their reach limited, meaning their posts will not be recommended to non-followers in Explore and Reels.
  • Appeals: Profile owners have the option to appeal if they are wrongly flagged.

💡 Why it matters

Instagram stated in a blog post, “We’ve heard that people don’t like seeing a profile that seems human, only to find out later that the person featured is AI-generated,” adding that users “want to know when a profile features an AI-generated person.”

🧩 How it works

User Type Label Requirement
AI-generated person Must self-label as an “AI-generated profile”
People using AI tools for content No label required

#Instagram #AI #SocialMedia #AIInfluencers

Source: Instagram cracks down on AI accounts pretending to be human
